districts.name: The Foundry
districts.purpose: The framework itself: the app class, the request context, middleware composition, the routers, the JSX renderer and the runtime adapters.

districts.name: Speed Trials
districts.purpose: Standalone packages that time the routers, JSX rendering and query parsing against other frameworks.

districts.name: Proving Grounds
districts.purpose: Integration suites that boot the framework on each supported runtime instead of mocking it.

districts.name: Instrument Yard
districts.purpose: Bundle size and type-check budgets recorded on every run so performance regressions show up as numbers.

districts.name: Knowledge District
districts.purpose: Contribution rules, the code of conduct and the migration guide; the user manual lives on a separate site.

buildings.role: The client-side renderer for the same JSX: hooks, context, memo and a DOM reconciler, exposed as the hono/jsx/dom entry point.
The JWT implementation behind the jwt and jwk middleware: signing, verification and the supported JWA algorithms, built on WebCrypto.
Static site generation: toSSG walks the app's routes, fetches each one and writes the responses to files, with hooks and route params.
Converts API Gateway, ALB and Function URL events into a Request and the Response back, with a streaming handler variant.
RegExpRouter, the fastest of the four: it compiles all routes into one regular expression, with a prepared variant built from serialised init params.
TrieRouter: it inserts each route into a node tree and searches that tree per request, and is used when routes are too dynamic to pre-compile.
The workerd adapter: static asset serving, WebSocket upgrade helpers and connection info for Cloudflare Workers.
One of the opt-in middlewares: secureHeaders sets Content-Security-Policy, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options and kin, and drops X-Powered-By.
The hono/bun entry point: static files read through Bun.file, WebSocket upgrade helpers, connection info, an SSG file system module and the Bun server object.
The type vocabulary: Env, Handler, MiddlewareHandler, Schema and the path-parameter inference the RPC client reads back.
The runtime-agnostic static file middleware; an adapter supplies getContent while this resolves paths, MIME types and precompressed variants.
createFactory and createMiddleware: typed constructors that keep the Env and path generics attached to handlers defined outside an app.
A router that keeps routes in a list and scans them in order, so registration stays cheap; the quick preset pairs it with the trie router.
The Context object handed to every handler: request access, response helpers and per-request state.
HonoBase: route registration, sub-app mounting, the default 404 and error handlers, and the fetch entry that dispatches a request.
The built-in JSX runtime used for server rendering and, through src/jsx/dom, on the client.
HonoRequest, the wrapper over the standard Request that exposes path params, parsed query, headers and validated body data.
The smallest router: one RegExp per route, matched in sequence, used where bundle size matters more than lookup speed.
The published package entry: it re-exports the Hono class plus the Context, HonoRequest and handler types an application needs.
SmartRouter: on the first request it replays the routes into each router it was given and keeps the first one that accepts them, then delegates to it.
Suspense plus renderToReadableStream, which sends fallback markup first and appends each resolved chunk as its promise settles.
The typed RPC client that mirrors a server's route types back to the caller.
The validator middleware: it reads one request target (json, form, query, param, header or cookie) and passes it to a validation function.
The Router interface every routing implementation satisfies; the seam that makes routing swappable.
HTTPException, thrown for fatal errors such as a failed authentication; it carries a status code and an optional Response.
Builds the onion-shaped middleware chain that wraps each matched handler.
The Hono application class, assembled from hono-base and the default router; this is what an app imports first.
The hono/tiny preset: the same app class pinned to PatternRouter, for size-constrained deployments.

ai.summary: Hono is an HTTP framework built on Web Standards. A small core in src (hono.ts, context.ts, compose.ts) sits behind four interchangeable router implementations, a large catalogue of opt-in middleware, and one adapter per runtime, so the same app runs on Bun, Deno, workerd, Lambda and Node.

strengths: The core is genuinely small: hono.ts, context.ts and compose.ts carry the framework and everything else is opt-in.
Routing is pluggable behind one Router interface, with four implementations and a smart router that chooses between them.
Runtime support is isolated in src/adapter, so a new platform is a new folder rather than a change to the core.
Tests sit beside the code as src/*.test.ts, and runtime-tests additionally boots the framework on Deno, Bun, Node, workerd, Fastly and Lambda.
Bundle size and type-check cost are measured in perf-measures on an ongoing basis, not just at release time.
concerns: The middleware catalogue and the adapters live in the same repository as the core, so the published surface is wide and every release moves all of it.
Almost the whole codebase sits under one src directory; the meaningful structure is a level deeper, which makes the top level look flatter than the project is.
The user-facing documentation lives on a separate site, so this repository's docs folder only covers contribution and migration.
